title: Peak velocity runway — regional GPU allocation & headroom targets (2026 Q3)
content:
Purpose: capture a concise runway plan for hosted API peak velocity events and define region-specific headroom targets (tokens/sec and QPS) tied to GPU family mix. This is a working sheet — assumptions and quick sims included.

High-level summary:
- Goal: ensure 99.9% availability for generation endpoints under historical peak+surge scenarios while minimizing overprovisioning for cost.
- Approach: define p95/p99 peak token rate by region, apply scenario multipliers (short burst / model rollout / sustained growth), convert to GPU slice targets by family (A100x, H100, and compact quantized slices), and codify headroom policy (percent over expected peak + buffer time for autoscale).

Assumptions (baseline):
- Observed historical p95 token/sec (global aggregated) in last 90d: 1.4M tokens/sec.
- Regional distribution (90d moving average): us-west 38%, us-east 30%, eu-west 18%, apac 9%, other 5%.
- Typical request mix: 60% short generates (<256 tokens), 30% medium (256–1024), 10% long (>1024).
- Preferred GPU families (production): H100 for low-latency queues, A100 for bulk throughput, q8_0 quantized slices for cost-sensitive routes.
- Effective tokens/sec per full GPU (mix-weighted): H100 120k tps, A100 85k tps, quantized slice (8-slice equivalent) 28k tps. (Derived from perf bench v2026.06).

Key scenarios and multipliers to apply to baseline peak: 
- Short extreme burst: 5 min, 4x baseline peak (rare; traffic storms from a viral event).
- Model rollout spike: 30 min, 2.5x baseline (auto-traffic upon new model release).
- Sustained seasonal peak: 3–6 hours, 1.6x baseline (marketing / event windows).
- Graceful degradation target: when capacity < headroom, fall back to 1) quantized model variant, 2) queued responses for non-interactive endpoints, 3) denylist non-critical customers.

Regional projection table (working):
Columns: Region | p95 tokens/sec (observed) | Scenario multiplier (planning) | Target planning tokens/sec | Headroom pct (policy) | Provisioned GPU equivalent (family mix notes)
us-west | 532000 | 1.6 (sustained) / 4.0 (burst) | 851200 (sustained) / 2.128M (burst) | 40% (sustained) / 80% (burst policy) | 7 H100 + 3 A100 + 4 q8_slices (sustained)
us-east | 420000 | 1.6 / 4.0 | 672000 / 1.68M | 40% / 80% | 5 H100 + 4 A100 + 3 q8_slices
eu-west | 252000 | 1.6 / 3.5 | 403200 / 882000 | 35% / 70% | 3 H100 + 3 A100 + 2 q8_slices
apac | 126000 | 1.6 / 3.5 | 201600 / 441000 | 35% / 70% | 2 H100 + 1 A100 + 1 q8_slice
other | 70000 | 1.5 / 3.0 | 105000 / 210000 | 30% / 60% | 1 H100 + 1 q8_slice

Notes on table: provisioned GPU equivalent rounds up to whole slices/pods to reflect scheduling constraints. For burst-level planning we recommend an on-call manual burst plan that uses cross-region capacity + pre-warmed reserved shards, rather than permanently maintaining burst-level headroom everywhere.

Headroom policy (recommended):
- Normal operating headroom: provision to p95 * scenario_multiplier(sustained) * (1 + headroom_pct_normal). Example: provision to sustained target + 35–40% headroom depending on region criticality.
- Emergency burst headroom: rely on reserved cross-region spillover + fast autoscale to increase slices. Only maintain 60–80% extra headroom in the largest region (us-west) by default.
- Autoscale warm-up buffer: maintain an internal 6–8 minute buffer (prewarm) where we keep additional cache-populated slices ready for sudden ramp; this maps to warm-up cost of ~1.2x token/sec overhead during the buffer window.

Prewarm and cache strategy:
- Keep a mini-pool of lightweight q8_slices across regions sized to absorb the first 30% of a burst (fast spin-up, low cost).
- If model variant differs (new model rollout), trigger a prewarm job to populate KV cache and warm tokenizers in target regions before cutover (automate via rollout pipeline).

Cost vs risk tradeoffs (quick sim):
- Holding sustained 40% headroom across global fleet increases monthly GPU cost by ~18% vs baseline but reduces incident MTTI and error budget burn by >70% in modeled spikes.
- Alternative: lean on cross-region spill and on-demand instances reduces steady cost but increases risk of degraded latency for 3–12 minutes during scale-up.

Operational playbook (short):
1) Detection: automated anomaly rule fires at 1.5x sustained target for >2 minutes (alert to infra oncall).
2) Immediate mitigation (0–5 minutes): redirect non-critical routes to quantized variants, increase q8 slice pool, enable burst routing to dedicated spare pool in us-west.
3) Scale (5–30 minutes): add H100/A100 slices per regional runbook, trigger cross-region spill if local capacity saturated.
4) Post-incident (30–120 minutes): run a short tailback test, analyze token burn and autoscale decisions, propose adjustments to headroom pct or prewarm timers.

SLA and SLO implications:
- Aim to maintain 99.9% availability for generation endpoints under sustained scenario multiplier of 1.6. For burst 4x, aim for graceful degradation guarantees (best-effort) and 95% availability for tier-1 customers via reserved pools.

Action items and owners (next steps):
- (Marta López) run a 7-day sensitivity sim for alternative GPU mixes (H100-heavy vs A100-heavy) and post results to RD-1234 — due 2026-07-19.
- (Samuel Green) prototype a q8 slice prewarm lambda that preloads KV for a rollout and measure warm-up time — due 2026-07-26.
- (Daniel Kim) update autoscaler policy to support 6-min warm-up window and test in staging — due 2026-08-02.

Open questions / discussion points:
- How aggressive should regional permanent headroom be for non-critical regions vs relying on cross-region spill?
- Should we maintain a small global 'burst reserve' (hot spare cluster) billed as reserved capacity? Cost/contract implications to finance.

Appendix — quick sensitivity notes:
- If average request length increases by 20% (model change), tokens/sec capacity requirement grows ~1.2x; headroom policy should be re-evaluated immediately.
- If quantized model performance degrades latency by >10% in production, fallback plan must be updated to avoid user-visible regressions.

End of working sheet. This doc should be iterated with infrastructure cost model and actual perf bench outputs (bench v2026.06).
